text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager — p99 inference latency breach (control-plane dependency)
Maya (oncall): paging in. seeing p95 ~420ms -> 1.2s, p99 spiking to 6-8s across multiple routes. streaming stalls reported. investigating.
Rafael (sre): I have the grafana panels up — spikes align with increase in control-plane auth error/backpressure. link: https://grafana.redwood/inference/slo?panel=controlplane-auth-latency
Lee (runtime): streaming tail latency jump correlated with KV cache miss ratio increasing. looks like config fetch/auth calls blocking the request path.
Maya (oncall): customer reports: some streaming connections stall mid-stream then resume (chunked), others reset. Dan, any incoming support tickets?
Dan (support): yes — two enterprise customers reported partial streaming stalls and a handful of 5xx on hosted API. I flagged as P1 and routed to SRE.
Priya (db): I'm seeing auth-sidecar 429s and a bunch of long-running SELECTs in the control-plane DB during the window. probable connection saturation + a burst of feature-flag checks. sample slow query: 
```sql
SELECT * FROM feature_flags WHERE org_id = $1 FOR UPDATE; -- 10s
```
Rafael (sre): also seeing increased 502/504 from control-plane endpoints in nginx logs: 
```
[2026-03-14T15:02:12Z] upstream_response_time: 8.3, status: 504, path: /v1/control/config/fetch
```
Lee (runtime): quick triage idea: route streaming traffic to fallback model-variant that uses fewer control-plane calls (no per-request feature flag checks). can we flip to soft-fallback?
Sasha (product): we should avoid blindly routing all traffic — keep canary to minimize customer impact. but agree we need to reduce control-plane dependency ASAP.
Maya (oncall): mitigation plan proposal: 1) enable local config cache on runtime nodes (ttl 60s) 2) temporarily disable remote feature-flag checks for streaming path (featureflag.check-external-auth = false) 3) scale auth-sidecar replicas x2 4) increase db connection pool for control-plane to handle burst 5) open communication to affected customers. agree?
Priya (db): scaling sidecar now. kubectl patch deployment auth-sidecar -n controlplane --replicas=4. increasing DB pool - applying settings to pool manager. watch for connection storms.
Rafael (sre): I'm going to add a short circuit on the control-plane client in runtime: fail-fast after 200ms and return cached decision to avoid head-of-line blocking. will push a hotfix to runtime with DeployBot.
DeployBot: Started deployment runtime/hotfix/controlpath-circuit (canary: 10%)
Lee (runtime): runtime hotfix rolling into 10% canary. config cache enabled locally via env: RUNTIME_CONFIG_CACHE_TTL=60
Dan (support): I'll send a targeted status update to affected customers: note streaming stalls, mitigation in progress, ETA 30-60m.
Sasha (product): add note to status page: partial degradation for streaming and increased latency for some routes.
Maya (oncall): quick logs show many 429s from auth service with header x-rate-limit-reason: auth-checks. can we relax rate-limiter for internal calls?
Priya (db): relaxing to allow burst from runtime nodes for next 15m. patched limiter to 2x burst. monitor.
Rafael (sre): post-mitigation metrics (5m after fixes): p95 down from 1.2s -> 320ms, p99 down from ~7s -> 900ms, error rate dropped from 3.6% -> 0.7%. streaming stalls largely reduced but a tail remains.
Lee (runtime): remaining tail looks like requests that hit a long-running DB lock on feature_flags. I'm going to deploy a one-off that routes those checks to a read-only replica and removes FOR UPDATE.
Priya (db): read replica routing enabled for non-critical reads. running: 
```bash
pgbouncer reload && export PG_RO_REPLICA=replica-02
```
Rafael (sre): ETA on full rollback of the temporary flags? we should keep conservative TTLs and circuit-breaker in place until next deploy.
Maya (oncall): keep circuit-breaker and cache for 2 hours, monitor SLOs. if stable, revert featureflag.disable after postmortem.
Dan (support): Customer update sent at 15:18: "We identified increased control-plane dependency causing streaming stalls and higher tail latency. We've applied mitigations — routing canary, local caching, scaled sidecars, and temporary rate-limit relax. Monitoring indicates improved performance. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline."
Sasha (product): filing postmortem and impact summary. priority: clarify why feature-flag checks escalated to FOR UPDATE and add defensive timeouts.
Priya (db): action items: 1) remove FOR UPDATE in feature flag path for read queries 2) add index on (org_id, flag_key) to avoid table scans 3) increase pool headroom for control-plane DB.
Rafael (sre): action items: 1) add circuit-breaker on control-plane client with exponential backoff 2) instrument per-route control-plane call counts 3) add alert for auth-sidecar 429 rate > 0.5%
Lee (runtime): action items: 1) keep local cache TTL 60s default, 2) add fallback model-variant policy for streaming path when control-plane unavailable 3) include backpressure metrics in runtime dashboard.
Maya (oncall): handing off to Rafael for follow-up and postmortem. leaving oncall.
Rafael (sre): taking handoff. creating incident doc with timeline and mitigations. will own RCA.
IncidentBot: Incident acknowledged and assigned to Rafael. severity: S1 (mitigated but customer impact).
Dan (support): I'll follow up with affected customers with the postmortem once available.
Sasha (product): thanks everyone — solid triage. we'll schedule a 1h RCA tomorrow to go over long-term fixes.
Maya (oncall): signing off now. final metrics snapshot: p95 310ms, p99 780ms, error rate 0.6%. will reopen if regressions appear.
